semantic_layer.runs: after the C11 parser and before the lowering, so a program that does not make sense never becomes machine code
semantic_layer.symbol_tables: a file scope, a function scope for the parameters, and a block scope for the locals; a lookup walks outwards, so a local may shadow an outer name, but a name may not be declared twice in the same scope
semantic_layer.types: the integer types with their signedness and widths, pointers, arrays, functions, structs and enums; a type lives in an arena that never moves it, because a type cannot hold itself
semantic_layer.declarators: resolved from the identifier outwards, so 'int *a[10]' is an array of pointers and 'int (*b)[10]' is a pointer to an array
semantic_layer.lvalues: an identifier, a subscript and a member are places that can be stored to; an assignment to anything else is reported
semantic_layer.calls: the number of the arguments is checked, and each argument is checked against its parameter
semantic_layer.returns: checked against the return type of the function
semantic_layer.diagnostics: every diagnostic carries the span of the source it is about, and the line and column

diagnostic_examples.message: the name "x" is declared twice in the same scope
the function "f" takes 2 arguments but 1 were given
this expression is not supported yet
a value of type X cannot be returned from a function that returns Y

findings.title: a function prototype is a file scope declaration, not a function declaration
findings.detail: the C11 parser records 'int helper(void);' as a DeclStmt whose VarDecl holds a declarator chain with a DeclaratorFunction; the layer recognises that chain, produces no code and treats the name as external
findings.consequence: a function may be declared in one translation unit and defined in another

findings.title: (void) is an empty parameter list, not a parameter of type void
findings.detail: counting the void parameter made a function that takes no arguments look as if it took one, and every call to it was reported
findings.consequence: fixed in both the declarator resolution and the function definition

unsupported_language_features: structs, unions and their member access
unsupported_abi_features: arguments are passed in the four integer registers only; a fifth argument would go on the stack, which is not implemented
the caller saved registers are never saved and never restored, because the lowering uses only volatile registers
the stack arguments of a variadic call are not set up
